JUDGMENT 1. Vide this judgment, I shall dispose off the present appeal filed by the appellant against the respondent.

The present appeal had been filed against the impugned order dated 17.02.2023 passed by the Ld.
Mahila Rohit Mehra Vs. Pooja Mehra Court, North whereby while disposing of application U/s 23 of PW DV Act, the appellant (respondent in the main case) was directed to make interim maintenance of Rs.25,000/- per month to the minor child from the date of filing of the petition.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. It is submitted by ld. Counsel for appellant that the ld. MM without appreciating submission of the appellant in the case has wrongly passed the impugned order in a mechanical manner without appreciating the evidence.
It is further submitted that respondent is earning Rs.84,000/- per month and able to maintain herself and the income of the appellant is Rs.65,000/-.
That the mother of the appellant is also dependent upon him.

sentences.text: 1 3. It is submitted by ld. Counsel for respondent that there is no illegality or infirmity in the impugned order.
It is further argued that the impugned order is passed in accordance with law and after taking all the material facts into consideration.
4. Brief facts of the case are that the complainant got married to appellant Rohit Mehra on 07.06.2014 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.
That one male child was born from the said wedlock, who is presently in the custody of respondent.

It is further alleged by the respondent that soon after marriage, she was subjected to cruelty at the hands of her husband (appellant) and his family members for demand of dowry and also her stridhan was misappropriated which was not returned despite specific demand Rohit Mehra Vs. Pooja Mehra and the complainant had filed criminal cases under Section 498A/406/34 IPC, under Section 12 D.V. Act and the application under Section 23 D.V. Act.

5. I have heard Ms. Dristi Mittal & Ms. Sudershani Ray, Ld. Counsels for the appellant and Mr.
Prateek Jindal, Ld. Counsel for respondent at length and perused the record carefully.

6. Vide the impugned order dated 17.02.2023 passed by Ld. Trial Court, considering the income affidavits of both the parties, Ld. Trial Court has observed that appellant/respondent no.1 (in the main case) was working as Manager in Genpact and on the basis if credit entries in his bank account his income is Rs.80,000/-, whereas the respondent i.e. complainant in the main case claimed that she is working as Manager in Sesame Workshop India Trust.
Bank account statement reflects that complainant got salary of Rs.55,500/- in March 2021, Rs.67,500/- in October and November 2021.
Bank account statement of January, February, march 2022 reveals that complainant received a salary of Rs.96,000/-.

She got salary of Rs.71,504/- in April, May, June, July, August, September,
October, December 2022 with additional credits of around Rs.5000/- in the month of June from her employer.
She further received an amount of Rs.1,11,282/- Rs.29,130/- in July 2022 Rohit Mehra Vs. Pooja Mehra which has gone unexplained.

entities.text: July 2022 Rohit Mehra Vs. Pooja Mehra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Apart from salary she received an amount of Rs.11,000/- from her employer in September 2022, Rs.24,000/- in October 2022, Rs.11,000/- in December 2022.
Further, she received a salary of Rs.90,000/- for the month of December 2022.
Thus, her salary is assessed at Rs.84,000/- per month.
Thus, without giving any findings on the merits of the case on the basis of the documents filed by the parties, Ld. Trial Court has assessed that both the parties are drawing almost similar income.
7. It was contended by the appellant that mother of the appellant is also dependent upon him.

However, though, mother of appellant is mentioned as dependent, she is not being considered as liability upon appellant as admittedly she is receiving Rs.17,000/- per month by way of pension and there are several credit entries as per which mother of appellant has transferred amount in the bank account of appellant.

Thus, it transpires that the salary of the appellant is to be divided amongst three portions i.e. himself, respondent/ complainant (in the main case) and the minor child, who is admittedly in the custody of the respondent herein.

8. Maintenance is not granted as a penalty but to ensure that the parties maintained a standard of living that is in close consonance with that enjoined by them as a family before Rohit Mehra Vs.
Pooja Mehra outbreak of their matrimonial discord.

sentences.text:
9. Now, coming to the judgment of Padmja Sharma Vs. Ratan Lal Sharma (2000) 4 SCC 266,
wherein it is held that in the present case both the parents are employed.

entities.text: Padmja Sharma Vs. Ratan Lal Sharma (2000) 4 SCC 266
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If we refer to the first application filed under Section 26 of the Act by the wife she mentions that she is getting a salary of Rs. 3,100 per month and husband is getting a salary of Rs. 5,850 per month.
She is, therefore, also obliged to contribute in the maintenance of the children.
Salaries of both the parents have since increased with the course of time.
We believe that in the same proportion, may be perhaps in the case of an employee of Reserve Bank of India at somewhat higher rate.
If we take approximate salary of husband is twice as much as that of the wife, they are bound to contribute for maintenance of their children in that proportion.
Family Court has already fixed a sum of Rs.. 250 per month for each of the child under Section 125 of the Code.
That amount we need not touch.

10. In view of the judgment of Padmja Sharma (Supra) both the parties are respectively to contribute proportionate maintenance to their child and solely burdening the Rohit Mehra Vs. Pooja Mehra appellant would not be appropriate at this stage.

As such as per case of Annurita Vohra Vs.
Sandeep Vohra 2004 (3) AD 252 the family income should be equally divided between the family members with one extra portion being allotted to the earning spouse, applying the said formula in the present case the family income is to be divided into 4 shares.

entities.text:
Annurita Vohra Vs.
Sandeep Vohra 2004 (3) AD 252
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The portion which should have been awarded to the child would be less than Rs.25,000/- i.e. 1/4th share of Rs.80,000/- assessed income of the appellant i.e. Rs.20,000/-.

Accordingly, it is directed that the impugned order dated 17.02.2023 is set aside to this extent and monthly expenses to the child should be Rs.20,000/- per month, to be paid by the appellant and respondent jointly and it is clarified that in case in future when the child goes to school or there is increase in his expenditure or unforeseen medical expenses etc. arise, respondent/complainant herein is at liberty to move appropriate application for enhancement before Ld. Trial Court, which may be dealt with in accordance with law.
11.
In view of the above discussion, the present appeal is allowed disposed off accordingly.
Both the parties are directed to appear before the Ld. Trial Court on 11.09.2023.
12. Nothing stated herein shall tantamount to an expression of opinion on the merits of the case.

Rohit Mehra Vs. Pooja Mehra 13. TCR, if any be sent back to the concerned court with copy of this order.
14.
Appeal file be consigned to record room.
